re_line: Trump-Putin-Xi APEC talk · Joshua Wong gets 10 more years · Huang summoned over China spy fears · yuan under strain
morning_memo: China confirmed contacts with Washington and Moscow over a possible Trump-Putin-Xi trilateral at the APEC summit in Shenzhen, the New York Times reported, with the gathering set for November 18-19.
Hong Kong sentenced democracy activist Joshua Wong to 10 more years in prison for foreign collusion, pushing his earliest release to late 2036.
Republican lawmakers asked Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang to brief Congress after reports he was targeted by Chinese intelligence, with Trump reportedly briefed on the findings roughly a year ago.

key_stat.label: PBOC's new rate for stock buyback re-lending
key_stat.context: The central bank cut the re-lending rate from 1.25% to 1% effective November 4, converting a temporary buyback-support facility into a permanent policy tool; more than 20 listed firms disclosed buyback plans citing the change.

prc_government.action: Opens anti-dumping probes into EU aramid fiber, vinylnorbornene imports
prc_government.detail: China launched anti-dumping investigations into imports of para-aramid filament yarn and vinylnorbornene originating in the European Union, per a November 6 notice.

prc_government.action: Cuts stock buyback re-lending rate, makes it a permanent tool
prc_government.detail: PBOC lowered its re-lending rate for stock buybacks and share increases from 1.25% to 1% effective November 4, 2026, shifting the facility from a stage-specific measure to a long-term institutional tool; over 20 listed companies announced buyback plans in response.

prc_government.ministry: Commerce Ministry + National Financial Regulatory Administration
prc_government.action: Seven ministries issue guidance on shipping insurance
prc_government.document: 《关于加快航运保险高质量发展的指导意见》
prc_government.detail: The National Financial Regulatory Administration, MOFCOM and five other departments jointly issued guidance to accelerate high-quality development of China's shipping insurance sector.

prc_government.action: Launches 'Shop in China · 2026 Premium Consumption Month'
prc_government.detail: MOFCOM kicked off a month-long domestic consumption promotion campaign aimed at spurring retail spending.

npc_politburo.detail: China's National People's Congress Standing Committee passed a cross-border anti-corruption law on November 6, comprising six chapters and 47 articles on international cooperation and legal liability, led by the National Supervisory Commission alongside foreign affairs, public security and finance departments, per Xinhua.

calendar_watch.headline: Busan-deal suspensions due to lapse
calendar_watch.detail: The one-year suspensions of BIS's Affiliates (50%) Rule and China's Oct 2025 rare-earth export controls, agreed at Busan, are due to expire unless extended.

calendar_watch.headline: APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting, Shenzhen
calendar_watch.detail: China hosts APEC November 18-19; a possible Trump-Putin-Xi trilateral is under discussion, per today's NYT report.

calendar_watch.headline: Taiwan nine-in-one local elections
calendar_watch.detail: Twenty-two mayors and magistrates and roughly 11,000 offices are up for election, read as a mid-term on President Lai Ching-te.

calendar_watch.headline: Nanjing Massacre National Memorial Day
calendar_watch.detail: 国家公祭日 falls amid continued China-Japan friction over Takaichi's Taiwan remarks.

calendar_watch.headline: G20 Leaders' Summit, Doral (Miami)
calendar_watch.detail: The US hosts the G20 December 14-15; Xi Jinping's attendance is unconfirmed.

overnight_items.headline: Shenzhen clears illicit chip and iPhone markets ahead of APEC
overnight_items.body_text: Shenzhen has cleared out illicit markets selling smuggled chips and stolen iPhones ahead of hosting the APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting November 18-19, the Financial Times reported. The cleanup targets the city's informal electronics trade before the gathering of international leaders.

overnight_items.headline: Hong Kong financial fiesta shows no doubt in the AI trade
overnight_items.body_text: No one at Hong Kong's annual financial conference doubted the AI trade, the Financial Times reported from the gathering. The sentiment contrasts with the global AI-driven selloff that has hit Asian tech and AI-linked stocks this week.

overnight_items.headline: China and Taiwan contest the legacy of Sun Yat-sen
overnight_items.body_text: China and Taiwan are contesting the historical legacy of Sun Yat-sen, the Economist reported, as both sides invoke the republic's founding father to bolster rival claims to political legitimacy. The dispute resurfaces periodically around cross-strait anniversaries and tensions.

overnight_items.headline: Chinese tech aids repressive African governments against dissent
overnight_items.body_text: Chinese-made surveillance and censorship technology is helping repressive African governments crush dissent, the Economist reported. The report details how exported Chinese tools are being used to monitor and suppress opposition movements across the continent.

overnight_items.headline: AFP debunks video falsely linked to India-China border tensions
overnight_items.body_text: AFP Fact Check found a viral video falsely linked to India-China border tensions actually showed a Nepali festival. The clip had circulated online with inaccurate claims about a border confrontation.

overnight_items.headline: Former Politburo member Ma Xingrui charged with bribery
overnight_items.body_text: Chinese prosecutors charged former Politburo member Ma Xingrui with taking bribes, the Washington Post reported November 4. The case marks the latest senior-level prosecution in Beijing's ongoing anti-corruption campaign.

overnight_items.headline: Taiwan, South Korea, Japan markets hit hard by AI selloff
overnight_items.body_text: Asian stock markets tied to the AI boom plunged Friday, led by Taiwan, South Korea and Japan, following an overnight tech selloff on Wall Street, Nikkei reported. The rout extended losses across chip and AI-linked names in all three markets.

overnight_items.headline: China's marriage rate hits 18-year low in third quarter
overnight_items.body_text: China's marriage registrations fell to an 18-year low in the third quarter, Reuters reported, extending a multi-year decline in nuptials. The drop compounds Beijing's challenge in reversing falling birth rates tied to marriage trends.

us_china.headline: Chinese AI lab Moonshot leases European chips to skirt US curbs
us_china.body_text: Chinese AI lab Moonshot AI has sought leasing agreements with 'neoclouds' in Europe to access Nvidia Blackwell chips, CNBC reported, circumventing US export restrictions on direct chip imports to China. The arrangement reflects continued efforts by Chinese AI firms to reach advanced US computing hardware despite the curbs.

us_china.headline: US escalates Cuba sanctions, designates two China-based suppliers
us_china.body_text: The US escalated its economic campaign against Cuba, designating two additional China-based suppliers, AP reported. China's Foreign Ministry said it 'firmly opposes' the sanctions and vowed to protect the legitimate rights of its companies, per a November 6 MOFA statement.

us_china.headline: Democrat-controlled Congress could force Taiwan arms sales resumption
us_china.body_text: A Democrat-controlled Congress could force **Donald Trump** to resume arms sales to Taiwan next year, said **Wu Xinbo**, dean at Fudan University's Institute of International Studies, after Tuesday's midterm sweep gave Democrats both chambers. Trump has delayed a *$14 billion* Taiwan arms package for months amid talks with Beijing.

us_china.headline: Binance hack funds flowed to Chinese launderers, Chainalysis finds
us_china.body_text: Funds from a Binance hack flowed to Chinese money launderers, blockchain analytics firm Chainalysis found, Bloomberg reported November 5. The finding adds to scrutiny of China-based networks laundering proceeds from crypto exchange breaches.

us_china.source: 美国之音中文 (VOA Chinese ZH)
us_china.headline: Taiwan defense minister: maintaining Congress contact on arms sales
us_china.body_text: Taiwan's Defense Minister **Wellington Koo** said the ministry is maintaining continuous communication with the US Congress to ensure arms sales proceed on schedule, per VOA Chinese. The comment comes as a *$14 billion* US arms package to Taiwan remains delayed months after approval.

china_world.headline: Taipei mayoral race framed as 'victory for democracy over China'
china_world.body_text: Taipei's mayoral race is 'a victory for democracy over China whoever wins,' a candidate told Reuters ahead of Taiwan's November 28 nine-in-one local elections. The remark frames the vote, covering 22 mayors and magistrates, against the backdrop of cross-strait pressure.

china_world.headline: MAC: 131 Taiwanese targeted by Chinese transnational repression since 2005
china_world.body_text: A total of *131* Taiwanese have been targeted a combined 149 times through Chinese transnational repression since 2005, Mainland Affairs Council Deputy Minister **Liang Wen-chieh** told a legislative session. The CCP has used nine methods including physical attacks, bounty-backed prosecutions, digital oppression and economic sanctions, he said.

china_world.headline: Beijing says Tokyo still 'dodging the issue' a year after Takaichi row
china_world.body_text: One year after Prime Minister **Sanae Takaichi's** Taiwan contingency remarks angered Beijing, foreign ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun said responsibility for the 'serious difficulties' in relations 'lay entirely with Tokyo,' per SCMP. Takaichi separately said Japan would pursue dialogue with China 'in the national interest,' per Kyodo.

china_world.headline: MOFCOM responds to EU fees on low-value imported goods
china_world.body_text: China's Commerce Ministry responded to the EU's move to impose additional fees on low-value imported goods, per a Chinese trade remedy information site. The response follows Brussels' push to curb a surge of low-cost parcels, many originating from Chinese e-commerce platforms.

china_world.headline: Xi Jinping holds talks with Oman's Sultan Haitham in Beijing
china_world.body_text: **Xi Jinping** held talks in Beijing with Oman's Sultan Haitham, according to China's embassy in the US. The meeting was part of a string of state visits Xi hosted this week, including Austria's chancellor and Gabon's president.

china_world.headline: Mexico's Sheinbaum flies to China to pursue meeting with Xi
china_world.body_text: Mexican President Sheinbaum is flying to China to pursue a meeting with **Xi Jinping** at the APEC summit, the Latin Times reported. Any Sheinbaum-Xi meeting would occur alongside the broader APEC gathering in Shenzhen November 18-19.

china_world.headline: Xi Jinping likely to skip ASEAN Summit in Manila, report says
china_world.body_text: **Xi Jinping** is likely to skip the ASEAN Summit in Manila, ANI News reported, citing unnamed sources. His potential absence would mark a departure from his attendance pattern at the annual regional gathering.

top_stories.headline: China in contact with US, Russia over possible Trump-Putin-Xi trilateral
top_stories.body: A possible trilateral summit bringing together **Xi Jinping**, **Vladimir Putin** and **Donald Trump** in China could bolster Xi's stature, but talks on Ukraine's future and limits on nuclear weapons would pose uncomfortable choices for Beijing, the New York Times reported November 6. The prospective summit is tied to China's hosting of the APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen November 18-19.

top_stories.headline: Hong Kong sentences Joshua Wong to 10 more years for foreign collusion
top_stories.body: Hong Kong sentenced democracy activist **Joshua Wong** to *10 more years* in prison on November 5 for colluding with foreign powers, the second time he has faced prosecution under the territory's National Security Law. Wong, 30, has already spent almost six years behind bars and is not due for release until late 2036.

top_stories.headline: Lawmakers summon Nvidia's Jensen Huang over Chinese spying concerns
top_stories.body: Top Republican lawmakers asked Nvidia CEO **Jensen Huang** to brief Congress after reports he was targeted by Chinese intelligence, the Financial Times and Reuters reported November 5. CNBC reported, citing the New York Times, that President **Trump** was briefed on the intelligence findings roughly a year ago.

top_stories.headline: China's 10-year yield hits record low as yuan dilemma deepens
top_stories.body: China's benchmark 10-year government bond yield hit a record intraday low on haven demand, Bloomberg reported November 6, as the global AI-driven equity selloff pushed investors toward safety. Reuters separately described a 'yuan dilemma' of the currency trading too weak offshore and too strong onshore, while the PBOC tweaked foreign-exchange reserve rules to help steady the yuan, the Wall Street Journal reported.

top_stories.headline: China confirms GJ-21 stealth drone's first shipborne takeoff, landing
top_stories.body: China's Ministry of National Defense confirmed the successful takeoff and landing of the **GJ-21** shipborne stealth drone at its early-November regular press briefing, calling it a milestone for new combat capabilities. The ministry spokesperson said China 'pursues a defensive defense policy.'

also_today.headline: China offshore market a 'value play' amid AI selloff, Nomura says
also_today.body_text: Nomura's Julia Wang said China's offshore market offers value amid the AI selloff, calling Taiwan's chipmaker 'irreplaceable' despite record index drops.

also_today.headline: Goldman Sachs: India, China H-shares offer refuge from AI selloff
also_today.body_text: Goldman's Tim Moe said India and China H-shares could outperform in the AI-driven selloff given lower exposure to tech hardware stocks.

also_today.headline: Goldman Sachs sees China internet stocks outperforming AI hardware names
also_today.body_text: Tim Moe said Chinese internet stocks could outperform AI hardware peers as investors reassess exposure amid narrowing losses.

also_today.headline: Beijing moves to bolster AI shares amid global tech selloff
also_today.body_text: AFP reported Chinese authorities are moving to support AI stocks as the sector slides amid a broader global technology selloff.

also_today.headline: Democrats' midterm sweep could dent China's AI-driven growth, BE says
also_today.body_text: Bloomberg Economics said the Democratic sweep of Congress could weigh on China's AI-propelled growth trajectory.

also_today.headline: Sinocism: Li Xi on Plenum resolution, CMG's post-Plenum propaganda push
also_today.body_text: Sinocism's roundup covered Li Xi's comments on the Plenum resolution and state media's post-Plenum propaganda work.

also_today.headline: Chinese firms' profit margins trail global peers on weak demand
also_today.body_text: Reuters reported Chinese companies' profit margins continue to lag global peers as domestic demand stays weak.

also_today.headline: Two Chinese nationals sentenced for illegal entry into Taiwan by dinghy
also_today.body_text: A Shilin court sentenced two Chinese men to nine and six months for crossing the Taiwan Strait by rubber dinghy in July.

also_today.headline: China to cut diesel exports on tight stocks, Energy Aspects says
also_today.body_text: Energy Aspects said China will cut diesel exports as domestic stockpiles run tight, Bloomberg reported.

business_economy.headline: Why China uses a 'national team' to influence stock trading
business_economy.body_text: Bloomberg examined how China's 'national team' of state-linked funds intervenes to influence stock trading, a mechanism deployed again this week amid the global AI-driven selloff.

business_economy.headline: China blocks SoftBank's $5.4bn bid for ABB's robotics unit
business_economy.body_text: China blocked SoftBank Group's *$5.4 billion* bid for ABB's robotics division, Bloomberg reported, citing the Financial Times. The move halts one of the largest recent cross-border robotics deals pending Chinese regulatory approval.

business_economy.headline: China's Q3 emissions post biggest drop since pandemic
business_economy.body_text: China's third-quarter carbon emissions posted their biggest drop since the pandemic as the Hormuz crisis curbed fossil fuel use, Reuters reported. Higher oil costs from the Middle East disruption pushed down fuel consumption across the quarter.

business_economy.headline: China's top flash memory chipmaker targets homegrown tools for new factory
business_economy.body_text: China's top flash memory chipmaker is targeting more homegrown toolmakers for its new factory, Reuters reported, reflecting Beijing's continued push for semiconductor equipment self-sufficiency amid US export controls.

business_economy.headline: German carmakers hit a 'dead end' as China drives past
business_economy.body_text: German carmakers have hit a dead end as Chinese rivals accelerate past them in home and export markets, AFP reported, describing mounting competitive pressure from Chinese EV makers.

business_economy.headline: Kimberly-Clark's China diaper woes linger despite steady outlook
business_economy.body_text: Kimberly-Clark's China diaper business continues to struggle, Reuters reported, though the company is standing by its full-year earnings outlook amid a separate controversy affecting the unit.

business_economy.headline: German wind industry faces €5.6 billion threat from China
business_economy.body_text: Germany's wind industry faces a *€5.6 billion* threat from Chinese competition, Bloomberg reported, citing industry estimates of potential losses to turbine makers as Chinese manufacturers expand in Europe.

official_line.speaker: Guo Jiakun
official_line.topic: China-Japan relations, one year after Takaichi's Taiwan remarks
official_line.statement: A year has passed, and Japan's authorities are still going in circles, still without showing the sincerity or taking the action needed to reflect on and correct their mistakes.
official_line.original_zh: 一年过去了，日本当局仍在原地打转，始终没有拿出反思纠错的诚意和行动
official_line.context: The statement marks one year since Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi's remarks on a Taiwan contingency, which Beijing says caused the current rift.
official_line.source: 外交部发言人 (MOFA presser ZH)

official_line.speaker: MOFA spokesperson
official_line.topic: US sanctions on Chinese firms over Cuba cooperation
official_line.statement: Per MOFA: China firmly opposes the new US sanctions on Chinese companies over Cuba cooperation and will take necessary measures to safeguard their legitimate rights and interests.
official_line.context: The comment followed Washington's designation of two additional China-based suppliers under its Cuba sanctions program.
official_line.source: 外交部发言人 (MOFA presser ZH)

official_line.speaker: MOFA spokesperson
official_line.topic: US-China trade relations and farm purchase commitments
official_line.statement: Per MOFA: China and the US must work toward each other to promote the sustained and steady improvement of economic and trade relations.
official_line.original_zh: 中美要相向而行，推动经贸关系持续稳定向好发展
official_line.context: The remark came amid questions over whether Washington would cut tariffs before Beijing fulfills its pledge to purchase US farm goods, a commitment from the May 2026 Trump-Xi summit.
official_line.source: 外交部发言人 (MOFA presser ZH)

official_line.speaker: MOFA spokesperson
official_line.topic: Canton Fair and CIIE as windows to the world
official_line.statement: Per MOFA: the Canton Fair and China International Import Expo held back-to-back are an important window for China to connect with the world.
official_line.original_zh: 是中国连接全球的重要窗口
official_line.context: The comment followed the opening of the ninth China International Import Expo days after the Canton Fair concluded.
official_line.source: 外交部发言人 (MOFA presser ZH)

official_line.speaker: TAO spokesperson
official_line.topic: Taiwanese firms at the ninth CIIE
official_line.statement: Per TAO: more than 30 Taiwanese enterprises will take part in the ninth China International Import Expo.
official_line.original_zh: 台湾30多家企业将参加第九届进博会
official_line.context: The announcement came as the ninth CIIE opened in Shanghai.

social_statements.quote_text: judges that Washington is distracted or that Trump would be willing to agree terms to not intervene
social_statements.analyst_note: Shearing's note was cited in Taipei Times reporting on how a Democrat-controlled Congress might affect Beijing's calculus toward Taiwan over the remaining two years of Trump's term.

social_statements.quote_text: The Chinese are very realistic that a new president might be very different (from Trump).
social_statements.analyst_note: Shen's comment was quoted in Sinocism's newsletter roundup, which also covered the Plenum resolution, post-Plenum propaganda work and Jensen Huang's reported China ties.

personnel_changes.name: Zhou Qian (周谦)
personnel_changes.detail: **Xi Jinping** signed a presidential order appointing Zhou Qian as China's ambassador to the Czech Republic, per Xinhua.

personnel_changes.position: Ambassador to Italy and San Marino
personnel_changes.name: Hou Yue (侯悦)
personnel_changes.detail: Hou Yue was appointed ambassador to Italy and San Marino under the same presidential order.

personnel_changes.position: Ambassador to New Zealand, Cook Islands and Niue
personnel_changes.name: Zhao Xing (赵星)
personnel_changes.detail: Zhao Xing was appointed ambassador to New Zealand, the Cook Islands and Niue.

personnel_changes.name: Ma Xingrui (马兴瑞)
personnel_changes.detail: Chinese prosecutors charged former Politburo member Ma Xingrui with taking bribes, the Washington Post reported November 4, part of Beijing's ongoing anti-corruption campaign.
